title: Why busy teams are slow
logline: Waiting time explodes as utilisation nears 100% — slack is what keeps work moving.
audience: Team leads and managers who plan capacity.

music.prompt: Minimal modern ambient, soft felt piano, warm analog pads, very light pulse

beats.visual: '90%' rises out of a mask on 'Ninety'; caption 'of capacity, booked' follows.

beats.vo: But waiting doesn't grow in a straight line.
beats.visual: Four bars — 50%, 80%, 90%, 95% busy — grow to 1×, 4×, 9×, 19× relative wait.

beats.vo: At half capacity, work waits one unit. At ninety percent, it waits nine.
beats.visual: The 90% bar takes the accent; others dim. Label: 9× the wait.

beats.vo: Leave slack. <short pause> It's what keeps work moving.
beats.visual: Title: 'Slack is not waste.' Source line: queueing theory, illustrative.

sources.claim: Relative wait ≈ ρ/(1−ρ): 1× at 50%, 4× at 80%, 9× at 90%, 19× at 95% utilisation
sources.source: Single-server queue (M/M/1) result — illustrative model, not measured data
